title: NGFS scenario families
facts: NGFS scenarios group into Orderly (Net Zero 2050, Below 2°C), Disorderly (Delayed Transition), Hot House World (Current Policies, NDCs), and Too-Little-Too-Late (Fragmented World).
Net Zero 2050 assumes immediate coordinated policy, ~1.4–1.5°C in 2100, high transition risk but low physical risk; Current Policies reaches ~3°C with severe physical risk.
NGFS Phase V (Nov 2024) updated damage functions — chronic physical damages materially higher than earlier phases.

title: Carbon price trajectories by scenario
facts: In NGFS Net Zero 2050, modelled global carbon prices reach roughly US$100–200/tCO2 by 2030 and several hundred by 2050 (model-dependent).
Delayed Transition scenarios show low prices this decade then a sharp spike after 2030 — the signature 'disorderly' shock to test in stress scenarios.
Use scenario carbon prices as shadow prices on Scope 1+2 to estimate EBITDA-at-risk.

title: Physical risk hazard set (IPCC AR6)
facts: Acute hazards: riverine/coastal flood, tropical cyclone, heatwave, wildfire, drought; chronic: sea-level rise, water stress, mean temperature rise, precipitation shift.
AR6 projects sea-level rise of ~0.28–0.55 m by 2100 under low emissions and ~0.63–1.01 m under very high emissions.
South Asia is a flagged hotspot for compounding heat-humidity risk; wet-bulb thresholds constrain outdoor labour productivity.

title: TCFD scenario analysis expectations
facts: TCFD (and IFRS S2 para 22) expect scenario analysis proportional to the entity's exposure, including at least one ≤2°C scenario, with disclosure of assumptions, time horizons and resilience conclusions.
Good practice pairs one orderly, one disorderly and one hot-house scenario, and quantifies impact on revenue, costs, and asset values by segment.

title: APRA CPS 229 climate risk expectations
facts: APRA's prudential guidance (CPG 229) expects regulated entities to embed climate risk in governance, risk appetite and scenario analysis; the Climate Vulnerability Assessment ran with the five largest banks.
AASB S2 reporting and APRA expectations interlock: scenario analysis capabilities built for CVA feed directly into mandatory disclosure.

title: Case study — Ørsted's transition
facts: Ørsted transformed from ~85% fossil-based heat & power (as DONG Energy) to ~90% renewable generation within a decade, divesting upstream oil & gas in 2017.
It is the textbook example of pre-empting stranded-asset risk by redirecting capex — cited in most transition-planning guidance.

title: GFANZ transition plan framework
facts: GFANZ recommends transition plans across five themes: foundations, implementation strategy, engagement strategy, metrics & targets, and governance.
Credible plans distinguish financing emissions reduction ('financed reductions') from portfolio decarbonisation via divestment, which shifts rather than cuts real-economy emissions.

title: TNFD and nature-related risk
facts: TNFD's final recommendations (Sept 2023) mirror TCFD's four pillars and add the LEAP process: Locate interface with nature, Evaluate dependencies/impacts, Assess risks/opportunities, Prepare to respond.
Priority sectors: agriculture, food, mining, energy, infrastructure and financial institutions exposed to them.

title: Case study — CBA climate scenario disclosure
facts: Commonwealth Bank's annual climate report discloses sector-level financed-emissions baselines and glidepaths, plus physical-risk maps of its mortgage book by postcode-level hazard exposure.
Mortgage-book flood/cyclone exposure analysis is the leading example of translating physical hazards into credit metrics for AASB S2.

title: MAS environmental risk management (Singapore)
facts: MAS ERM Guidelines (2020) require banks, insurers and asset managers to embed environmental risk in governance, risk management and disclosure, with board-level accountability.
MAS industry stress tests have included long-run climate scenarios aligned to NGFS pathways; disclosure expectations reference TCFD/ISSB alignment.
